intro_stillness.text:
Before anything else —

— a moment of stillness.

intro_breath.text:
There is no urgency here.

This is not a test. There are no correct answers.

There is only looking.

choices.label: I am my name — the person the world knows.
I am what I do — my work, my role.
I am my relationships — defined by those I love.
I don't know.

l1_name_probe.text:
It was given to you before you could speak. Before you could agree or disagree.

If tomorrow everyone knew you by a different name — everything else the same — would you still be you?

choices.label: Yes. The name is just a label.
Something would feel different.

l1_name_yes.text:
Then the name is not you. It is something you carry.

A label attached to something that existed before the label arrived.

l1_name_different.text:
Perhaps. We grow attached to names. They become familiar.

But notice: the attachment is yours. The name is not.

Something in you knows the difference between the label and the one wearing it.

l1_profession_response.text: What you do. Your work. Your function in the world.

l1_profession_probe.text:
When you were a child — before any profession, before you could do anything useful — were you less real?

Were you less yourself?

choices.label: I was different then, but still myself.
I felt more whole when I had purpose.

l1_profession_same.text:
Then what you do is not what you are.

The profession arrived. The one who noticed it arriving was already there.

l1_profession_different.text:
Purpose gives shape to things. But notice: even the child without purpose was watching, feeling, existing.

Something persisted through every change in what you did.

That something is closer to you than your work.

l1_relation_response.text:
Your relationships. Son, daughter, parent, friend, partner.

These exist in relation to others.

l1_relation_probe.text: When you are truly alone — no one watching, no relationship active — are you still there?

choices.label: Yes. I exist independently of others.
I feel incomplete when I am alone.

l1_relation_yes.text:
Then you exist prior to the relationships.

They describe how you connect to others — not what you are.

l1_relation_incomplete.text:
That incompleteness is worth sitting with.

Is it the relationship that makes you complete — or is it the feeling of being seen?

Those are different things. The first is about others. The second is about something in you.

l1_unknown_response.text:
That is the most honest answer in this room.

Most people rush to fill that space. You did not.

l1_unknown_probe.text: When someone asks who you are — in the world, in daily life — what do you usually say?

choices.label: My name, my job, something social.
I deflect, or change the subject.

l1_unknown_social.text:
Of course. That is the functional answer. It works in context.

But you already sensed it was not the full answer. That sensing — that too is you.

The one who knows the answer is incomplete.

l1_unknown_deflect.text:
The deflection is interesting.

Something in the question feels dangerous — as if a real answer would expose something.

What is it that is being protected? That too is worth looking at.

l1_convergence_a.text: Everything you named — name, role, relationship — was placed on you, or arose through circumstances you did not choose.

l1_convergence_b.text:
You did not choose your family. Your country. The language that shaped your first thoughts.

Even your fears and desires largely arrived before you were old enough to examine them.

l1_convergence_c.text:
This does not make them unreal.

But it raises a question: are these things you — or things that happened to you?

l1_to_l2_transition.text:
Let us go a little deeper.

There is something more intimate than a name or a role. Something that feels like 'you' from the inside.

l2_question.text:
In the space between who you show the world and who you feel yourself to be —

what do you most want people to see in you?

choices.label: That I am capable. That I can do things well.
That I am good. That I genuinely care.
That I am reliable. That others can count on me.
Nothing. I do not need others to see anything in me.

l2_achiever_1.text:
Capability. The drive to build, to master, to achieve.

There is real dignity in this. And also — something worth examining.

l2_achiever_2.text:
Imagine you have achieved everything you set out to achieve. Recognition. Success. Mastery.

Then what?

choices.label: I would be satisfied.
I would set new goals.
I am not sure.

l2_achiever_satisfied.text:
Have you ever achieved something and felt that satisfaction last?

For how long, usually?

Notice what happens after the satisfaction fades. What is the texture of that feeling?

l2_achiever_new_goals.text:
So the goal was never the destination. The moving itself is the need.

What is it that needs to keep moving? What happens — inside — if the moving stops?

l2_achiever_unsure.text:
That uncertainty is worth staying with.

Perhaps the achievement was never really the point.

Perhaps it was a way of answering a question that the achievement itself could never actually answer.

l2_achiever_mirror.text:
When you strip away the achievement — when nothing external confirms your worth —

who are you then?

Is there anyone there?

l2_approval_1.text:
Goodness. Being seen as someone who genuinely cares.

There is real warmth in this impulse. And also — a question worth asking.

l2_approval_2.text:
Is there a version of you that exists when no one is watching?

A self that is real even when unseen?

choices.label: Yes — I am the same alone as I am with others.
I feel less defined when I am alone.

l2_approval_same.text:
Then your goodness does not depend on being witnessed.

But notice: the wanting to be seen as good — where does that come from?

What would happen inside you if others thought you were not good, regardless of what you did?

l2_approval_less.text:
That is an honest and important observation.

The self that exists primarily in others' eyes — is that the self you want to be?

Or is there something underneath, waiting to be seen by you first — before anyone else?

l2_approval_mirror.text:
The need to be seen as good is often a response to an earlier fear.

The fear that without approval — without being good enough — you would not be enough.

Is that fear still here? Right now, in this space?

l2_protector_1.text:
Reliability. The one who holds things together.

There is real strength in this. And — something worth examining.

choices.label: The people I love.
A sense of order. Stability.

l2_protector_people.text:
And if the people you protect no longer needed your protection — or if they were no longer there —

who would you be?

Is the protector the real you, or a role that was taken on — and then never put down?

l2_protector_order.text:
Order, stability. These are valuable.

But notice: they are maintained against a background of constant change. Everything changes. Nothing stays assembled forever.

What is it that fears the change? Is that fear you?

l2_protector_mirror.text:
The protector pattern is often built over an old wound.

Something once felt unsafe. And a part of you decided: never again.

That decision made sense then. But it has been making choices on your behalf ever since. Without asking.

l2_awareness_1.text:
Nothing from others' perception. A clean answer.

Or perhaps — it is a pattern of its own. The one who is beyond needing.

l2_awareness_2.text:
Is this freedom from others' opinions genuine?

Or is it a kind of armor — a way of not being hurt?

choices.label: I think it is genuine.
Perhaps there is some defense in it.

l2_awareness_genuine.text:
Then you have moved past most of what this layer tests.

But notice: even 'the one who is beyond needing' is still an identity. Still a position the self takes.

Who is the one who is beyond needing?

l2_awareness_defense.text:
That honesty is rare. And valuable.

The one who protects themselves by needing nothing — what would happen if they allowed themselves to need?

What is the fear underneath the independence?

l2_convergence_pattern.text:
You have been [PATTERN] for a long time.

Not as a flaw. It emerged for reasons — probably good reasons, at some point.

l2_pattern_mechanic.text:
This pattern has a simpler name: the ego. Not arrogance — just the structure that decided, long ago, who it needs to be.

Notice: it makes choices before you do.

When a situation arrives, it has already decided the shape of your response — before you have had a chance to see clearly.

The question is not whether the pattern is good or bad.

l2_pattern_question.text:
The question is: is this the chooser you want to be?

Or is there something prior to the pattern — something that could actually see, and then choose?

transition_to_silence.text: You do not have to answer that.

silence_1.text: There is no next question here.

silence_2.text:
Just for a moment — notice what is here.

Not what you think about it. Just what is.

silence_3.text:
The one who is noticing this —

that is closer to you than anything named today.

end_session.text:
That is where we stop for now.

Not because the inquiry is complete. It is not.

Real inquiry cannot be sustained through a screen. It continues in you — in the quiet moments, in the gaps between thoughts.

end_return.text: If you want to continue looking —
